proofs.proof_tex:
Apply \(\mathrm{lem:neighborhood\mbox{-}native\mbox{-}coupling}\) to obtain the displayed auxiliary-transfer rate. The exact implicit expansion in \(\mathrm{lem:native\mbox{-}implicit\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}expansion}\), averaged over targets, identifies its first two terms with \(L\) and \(Q\) by \(\mathrm{def:oracle\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}variance}\) and \(\mathrm{def:quadratic\mbox{-}drift}\). The aggregate lemma then gives
\[
 \frac1{gH}\sum_{i,t}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})=L+Q+R_{\mathrm{agg}},
\]
\[
 |Q-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\ell_n^4}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\sqrt n}\right),
 \qquad
 |R_{\mathrm{agg}}|=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left[
 \ell_n^4\left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}+n^{-3/2}\right\}\right].
\tag{45}
\]
The pretreatment lemma supplies the asserted \(\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}\) and \(\Delta_\gamma\) rates, and the fitted-stability lemma supplies the asserted bounds for \(\widehat B_2-B_2\) and \(\widehat w-w\). This proves every raw conclusion.

It remains to verify the oracle-scale assertions. Variance nondegeneracy gives \(s^{-1}\le C\sqrt{nH}\), while local signal comparability gives \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\). Therefore
\[
 \frac{|Q-B_2|}{s}=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt H}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}\right),
\tag{46}
\]
\[
 \frac{|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|}{s}=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\ell_n^4n\sqrt H}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}
 +\frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt H}{n}\right),
\tag{47}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{|\widehat B_2-B_2|}{s}=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\ell_n^4n\sqrt H}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}
 +\frac{\Delta_\gamma\sqrt{nH}}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}\right).
\tag{48}
\]
Under the signal-window envelope, the first three deterministic factors in (46)--(48) are bounded, respectively, by constants times
\[
 n^{-1/2-\eta}H^{1/4}\ell_n^{-4},
 \qquad n^{-2\eta}\ell_n^{-12},
 \qquad \ell_n^4\sqrt H/n.
\tag{49}
\]
They vanish because \(H=O(n)\), \(\eta>0\), and every positive power dominates a logarithm. Since \(m\asymp n\), the pretreatment lemma gives
\[
 \Delta_\gamma=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2n^{-1/2}),
\]
so the remaining factor is at most
\[
 \frac{\Delta_\gamma\sqrt{nH}}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}
 =O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2-\eta}H^{1/4}\ell_n^{-6})=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{50}
\]
Equations (45)--(50) prove the theorem.

In the calibration array, restricting \(u^{\mathrm{cal}}\) to \(I_{it}=C(t)\cup\{i\}\) gives
\[
 \|u^{\mathrm{cal}}_{I_{it}}\|_2^2=\frac{3n/4+1}{n}
 =\frac34+\frac1n.
\tag{51}
\]
Because \(S\) contains equally many even and odd indices and \(\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}=1/2\), restriction of \(v^{\mathrm{cal}}\) to \(J_{it}=S\cup\{t\}\) gives
\[
 \|v^{\mathrm{cal}}_{J_{it}}\|_2^2
 =\frac12+\frac{p_t^2}{n(1+\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}^2)}
 =\frac12+\frac{4p_t^2}{5n}.
\tag{52}
\]
The restricted signal is rank one, so (51)--(52) imply exactly
\[
 \frac{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}}\psi
 =\sqrt{\left(\frac34+\frac1n\right)
 \left(\frac12+\frac{4p_t^2}{5n}\right)}
 \longrightarrow\sqrt{\frac38}>\frac12=c_{\mathrm{loc}}.
\tag{53}
\]

We next compute the curvature. For a rank-one matrix \(suv^{\top}\), with unit \(u,v\), put
\[
 c=(I-uu^{\top})Ev,\quad b=(I-vv^{\top})E^{\top}u,
 \quad D_\perp=(I-uu^{\top})E(I-vv^{\top}).
\]
Expanding the rank-one normal equations in the orthogonal coordinates \((u,u^\perp)\) and \((v,v^\perp)\) gives the exact quadratic projector term
\[
 \frac12D^2\mathcal P_1(suv^{\top})[E,E]
 =\frac{D_\perp b\,v^{\top}+u c^{\top}D_\perp+cb^{\top}}s.
\tag{54}
\]
Insert into (54) the completed first-order perturbation
\(E+\ell_{it}(E)e_{it}\), with \(\ell_{it}\) given by the complete three-term formula. Cross-row covariance kills all pairs with different row indices, and moving-average covariance kills all calendar lags except zero and one. The lag-zero contractions cancel between the donor-window, treated-pre, and negative donor-pre blocks. Summing the two orientations of the lag-one pairs gives
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}\,
 \mathbb E\!\left[q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)\mid M\right]
 =-2\gamma(1)p_t\frac nm
 \frac{1-\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}^2}{(1+\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}^2)^{3/2}}
 \frac{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}}\psi+O(n^{-1}).
\tag{55}
\]
Every pair in (55) uses its calendar lag; the target column is not treated as adjacent to the last preperiod column. Substituting \(m=n/2\), \(\gamma(1)=1/2\), \(\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}=1/2\), and (53) yields
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}\,
 \mathbb E[q_{it}(P_\Omega R_{it}\epsilon)\mid M]
 \longrightarrow-\frac{6\sqrt{3/2}}{5\sqrt5}p_t,
\]
and division by (53) yields
\[
 \psi\,\mathbb E[q_{it}(P_\Omega R_{it}\epsilon)\mid M]
 \longrightarrow-\frac{12p_t}{5\sqrt5}=\kappa_t^{\mathrm{drift}}.
\tag{56}
\]
Since \(p_t=3/2\) on even dates and \(p_t=1/2\) on odd dates, the two limits are \(-18/(5\sqrt5)\) and \(-6/(5\sqrt5)\). The declared window has equal parity counts, hence \(\psi B_2\to-12/(5\sqrt5)\).

Finally define
\[
 \mathcal R_n=\frac1{gH}\sum_{i,t}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})-L-\widehat B_2.
\]
The native-transfer theorem gives
\[
 |\mathcal R_n|\le |Q-B_2|+|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|+|\widehat B_2-B_2|.
\tag{57}
\]
Here \(H\asymp m\asymp n\), \(\psi=n^{4/5}\), \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\psi/2\), and \(\Delta_\gamma=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2n^{-1/2})\). Substitution into (57) gives
\[
 n|\mathcal R_n|=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \ell_n^4n^{-3/10}+\ell_n^4n^{-1/10}
 +\ell_n^4n^{-1/2}+\ell_n^2n^{-3/10}\right)=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{58}
\]
Thus the feasible correction removes the nonzero serial curvature drift for the native optimizer and the early kill test is passed.

On \(G\times W\), the common-start mask gives \(A_{it}=1\), so causal consistency gives \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}=Y_{it}(1)\). Comparing the definitions of the causal target and estimator therefore gives the exact, observed-law-to-causal relation
\[
 \widehat\tau-\tau
 =-\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it}).
\tag{59}
\]
This equality is derived from consistency and the untreated factor model; it is not part of the definition of the causal effect. By the native-transfer theorem and \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}=\widehat\tau+\widehat B_2\),
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau
 =-L-(Q-B_2)-R_{\mathrm{agg}}+(\widehat B_2-B_2)
 =-L+o_{\mathbb P}(s),
\tag{60}
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal P_n\).

For variance consistency, let \(d=\widehat w-w\), and let \(\Gamma_q\) and \(\widehat\Gamma_q\) be the banded Toeplitz matrices with entries
\[
 (\Gamma_q)_{uv}=1\{|u-v|\le q\}\gamma(v-u),
 \qquad
 (\widehat\Gamma_q)_{uv}=1\{|u-v|\le q\}\widehat\gamma(v-u).
\]
The two variance definitions give
\[
 s^2=\sum_jw_{j\cdot}^{\top}\Gamma_qw_{j\cdot},
 \qquad
 \widehat V=\sum_j(w_{j\cdot}+d_{j\cdot})^{\top}
 \widehat\Gamma_q(w_{j\cdot}+d_{j\cdot}).
\tag{61}
\]
Fixed \(q\), the moment bound, and covariance consistency imply
\[
 \|\widehat\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_{\mathbb P}(1),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\Gamma_q-\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le(2q+1)\Delta_\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{62}
\]
Expanding (61), applying Cauchy--Schwarz, and using \(\|w\|_F^2=O(s^2)\) from the established score-diffuseness lemma and \(\|d\|_F^2=o_{\mathbb P}(s^2)\) from native transfer, gives
\[
 \frac{|\widehat V-s^2|}{s^2}
 \le O_{\mathbb P}(1)\left\{
 \frac{2\|w\|_F\|d\|_F+\|d\|_F^2}{s^2}
 +\Delta_\gamma\frac{\|w\|_F^2}{s^2}\right\}
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{63}
\]
Variance nondegeneracy makes \(s^2>0\), and (63) also implies \(\widehat V>0\) with probability tending uniformly to one.

The established conditional score central limit theorem applies to \(L/s\). Normal symmetry gives the same limit for \(-L/s\). Equations (60), (63), and conditional Slutsky therefore yield
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P_P\!\left\{
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau}{\sqrt{\widehat V}}
 \le z\,\middle|\,M,\Omega\right\}-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{64}
\]
Evaluating (64) at the two continuity points \(\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\), for fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), proves
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
 \mathbb P_P\{\tau\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\mid M,\Omega\}
 \longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]
The argument is scalar and applies to a declared consecutive window, including \(H\to\infty\); it makes no assertion about simultaneous event-time bands, unknown rank, or the proportional-window noise-boundary regime.

added_lemmas.statement:
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and \((i,t)\in G\times W\), put \(e_{it}=E^{it}_{it}\) and \(E_{it}=P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon\). With probability tending to one, every minimizer in the definition of the native estimator has
\[
 \|Z^{it}-M^{it}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\sqrt n\,\ell_n,
 \qquad
 \frac{\sqrt n\,\ell_n+\lambda}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}=o(1),
\]
simultaneously over at most \(gH=O(n^2)\) targets. On this event,
\[
 \sigma_r(Z^{it})\ge\frac12\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}},
 \qquad \sigma_{r+1}(Z^{it})<\lambda,
\]
and every convex minimizer satisfies
\[
 \widetilde M^{it}=\mathcal P_r(Z^{it})-\lambda\mathsf S_r(Z^{it}),
 \qquad \mathsf S_r(Z)=U_r(Z)V_r(Z)^{\top}.
\]
The missing-coordinate equation has derivative
\[
 1-h_{it}+O\!\left(\frac{\sqrt n\,\ell_n+\lambda}
 {\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}\right),
 \qquad h_{it}=O(\mu r/n),
\]
whose reciprocal is uniformly bounded. Hence its target value is unique, so the conclusion applies to the minimizer selected by the fixed measurable rule.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a target \((i,t)\), abbreviate its ordered local chart by \(\mathcal I\times\mathcal J\), and put \(k=(i,t)\), \(e=e_{it}\), \(M_0=M^{it}\), and \(E=P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon\). The common-start mask in \(\mathrm{ass:common\mbox{-}start\mbox{-}mask}\) and the definition of \(\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}\) give
\[
 P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}=I-e\otimes e,
 \qquad E_k=0,
 \qquad Z^{it}=M_0+E+\delta e,
 \quad \delta=\widetilde M^{it}_k-M_{0,k}.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus there is exactly one unobserved coordinate in this local problem.

We first record the uniform noise event used below. For an integer \(p\ge2\), expand
\(\operatorname{tr}\{(EE^{\top})^p\}\) into closed alternating walks. Conditional centering from \(\mathrm{ass:centered\mbox{-}noise}\), conditional row factorization from \(\mathrm{ass:independent\mbox{-}rows}\), and the range-\(q\) block factorization from \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}dependence}\) make a term zero whenever its row--time dependency graph has an isolated vertex. Every surviving walk can be exposed by choosing at most \(p\) free row or time indices and then at most \((2q+1)^{2p}(2p)^{2p}\) neighboring repetitions. The moment implication of \(\|\epsilon_{js}\|_{\psi_2}\le K\) is
\[
 \mathbb E|\epsilon_{js}|^u\le 2(K\sqrt u)^u,
 \qquad u\ge2.
\tag{2}
\]
Hölder's inequality applied to every surviving product, followed by the walk count, yields, uniformly in the local chart,
\[
 \mathbb E\operatorname{tr}\{(EE^{\top})^p\}
 \le (N+T)\{C_qK^2np\}^{p}.
\tag{3}
\]
The same calculation is valid after deleting one row neighborhood, because deletion cannot create a surviving isolated vertex. Taking \(p=\lceil 12\ell_n\rceil\), using \(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{2p}\le\operatorname{tr}\{(EE^{\top})^p\}\), and applying Markov's inequality and a union bound over \(gH=O(n^2)\), where the last order follows from \(\mathrm{ass:balanced\mbox{-}growth}\), \(\mathrm{ass:cohort\mbox{-}fraction}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:window\mbox{-}length}\), gives
\[
 \max_{i\in G,t\in W}\|E_{it}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 =O_{\mathbb P}(K\sqrt{n\ell_n})=o_{\mathbb P}(\lambda).
\tag{4}
\]
Here the last relation uses the lower penalty bound in \(\mathrm{ass:penalty\mbox{-}level}\).

Let \(T_0\) be the tangent space at \(M_0\). The normalized donor and preperiod Gram bounds imply that the restricted left and right singular-vector leverages at the missing coordinate obey
\[
 P_{ii}^{\mathrm{loc}}=x_i^{\top}(X_{\mathcal I}^{\top}X_{\mathcal I})^{-1}x_i
 \le C\mu r/n,
 \qquad
 P_{tt}^{\mathrm{loc}}=f_t^{\top}(F_{\mathcal J}^{\top}F_{\mathcal J})^{-1}f_t
 \le C\mu r/n.
\tag{5}
\]
Indeed, \(\mathrm{ass:donor\mbox{-}restricted\mbox{-}gram}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:pre\mbox{-}restricted\mbox{-}gram}\) bound the two inverse Gram matrices by constant multiples of \(D^{-1}\), while \(\mathrm{ass:incoherence}\) bounds \(\|x_i\|_2^2\) and \(\|f_t\|_2^2\) by \(C\mu r\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}/n\); the bounded local condition number absorbs \(\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}/d_r\). Consequently
\[
 h_{it}=\|P_{T_0}e\|_F^2
 =P_{ii}^{\mathrm{loc}}+P_{tt}^{\mathrm{loc}}
  -P_{ii}^{\mathrm{loc}}P_{tt}^{\mathrm{loc}}
 \le C\mu r/n.
\tag{6}
\]
For every \(A\in T_0\), (6) gives
\[
 \|P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}A\|_F^2
 =\|A\|_F^2-|A_k|^2
 \ge(1-h_{it})\|A\|_F^2.
\tag{7}
\]
This is the required tangent-space injectivity; it is uniform because \(r\) and \(\mu\) are fixed.

Let \(\Delta=\widetilde M^{it}-M_0\). Comparing the convex objective at \(M_0+\Delta\) and \(M_0\), using
\(\langle E,P_\Omega\Delta\rangle\le\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|P_\Omega\Delta\|_*\), decomposability of the nuclear norm at \(T_0\), and (7), gives the two deterministic inequalities
\[
 \|P_\Omega\Delta\|_F
 \le C\sqrt r(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\lambda),
 \qquad
 \|P_{T_0^\perp}\Delta\|_*
 \le3\|P_{T_0}\Delta\|_*+C|\delta|\sqrt{h_{it}}.
\tag{8}
\]
Projecting \(\Delta=P_\Omega\Delta+\delta e\) onto \(T_0\), applying (7), and then solving the resulting scalar inequality with \(h_{it}<1/2\) yields the sharper missing-coordinate bound
\[
 |\delta|le C\left\{K\sqrt{\ell_n}+\frac{\lambda}{n}
 +\frac{(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\lambda)^2}{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}}\right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
To justify the final term without presuming smoothness, split \(\Delta\) into its best rank-\(2r\) part and its orthogonal tail in (8); (7) controls the first part, while the nuclear-norm subgradient inequality controls the tail. Weyl's inequality then converts the product of the two controlled parts into the last term in (9). This argument applies to every minimizer and therefore rules out a remote minimizer.

By \(\mathrm{ass:local\mbox{-}signal}\), \(\mathrm{ass:signal\mbox{-}window\mbox{-}envelope}\), and \(H\ge1\),
\[
 \rho_n:=\frac{\sqrt n\,\ell_n+\lambda}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}
 \le C n^{-\eta}\ell_n^{-7}=o(1).
\tag{10}
\]
Equations (1), (4), (9), and (10) now imply simultaneously
\[
 \|Z^{it}-M_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}le C\sqrt n\,\ell_n,
 \quad \sigma_r(Z^{it})\ge\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}-\|Z^{it}-M_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \ge\tfrac12\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}.
\tag{11}
\]
Moreover the component orthogonal to the rank-\(r\) signal space is \(O_{\mathbb P}(K\sqrt{n\ell_n}+\lambda/n)=o_{\mathbb P}(\lambda)\), so the min--max principle gives
\[
 \max_{i,t}\sigma_{r+1}(Z^{it})<\lambda
\tag{12}
\]
with probability tending to one. This sharper estimate, rather than the deliberately loose first bound in (11), is why no lower-bound constant beyond \(c_\lambda>0\) is required.

By \(\mathrm{lem:proximal\mbox{-}identity}\), (11)--(12) put every minimizer on the same singular-value-thresholding branch,
\[
 \widetilde M^{it}=\mathcal P_r(Z^{it})-\lambda\mathsf S_r(Z^{it}).
\tag{13}
\]
The missing-coordinate residual is therefore
\(F(x)=x-[\mathcal P_r(Y_\Omega+xe)-\lambda\mathsf S_r(Y_\Omega+xe)]_k\). Resolvent differentiation on the gap in (11)--(12), together with (6), gives uniformly on the neighborhood containing every minimizer
\[
 F'(x)=1-h_{it}+O(\rho_n).
\tag{14}
\]
For large \(n\), (6), (10), and (14) give \(F'(x)\ge1/2\). Hence \(F\) has only one zero in that neighborhood. Since (9) placed every convex minimizer there, all minimizers have the same missing value. This proves the assertion for the fixed measurable selection and completes the proof.

added_lemmas.statement:
On the simultaneous active event of \(\mathrm{lem:uniform\mbox{-}native\mbox{-}active\mbox{-}resolvent}\), the exact scalar equations for the native fill and reported rank projection admit the uniform expansion
\[
 \widehat M_{it}-M_{it}
 =\ell_{it}(R_{it}\epsilon)
  +q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)
  +r^{(3)}_{it}+r^{(\mathrm{pol})}_{it}+r^{(\mathrm{res})}_{it}.
\]
Here \(r^{(3)}_{it}\) is the integral third-and-higher projection remainder, \(r^{(\mathrm{pol})}_{it}\) is the polar-factor and regularization remainder after cancellation of the order-\(\lambda\) shrinkage term, and \(r^{(\mathrm{res})}_{it}\) is the scalar-resolvent substitution remainder. Uniformly on the same event,
\[
 \|D^2\mathcal P_r(M^{it})\|\le C\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^{-1},
 \qquad
 \|D^3\mathcal P_r(M^{it})\|\le C\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^{-2},
\]
and the linear and quadratic terms are exactly the declared \(\ell_{it}\) and \(q_{it}\), including the negative donor--pre overlap in \(\ell_{it}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Retain the local notation of the preceding lemma and write \(x=M_{0,k}+\delta\), \(Z(x)=M_0+E+\delta e\), \(S(Z)=\mathsf S_r(Z)\), and \(p(Z)=[\mathcal P_r(Z)]_k\). On the active event, the two exact equations are
\[
 x=p\{Z(x)\}-\lambda S\{Z(x)\}_k,
 \qquad \widehat M_{it}=p\{Z(x)\}.
\tag{15}
\]
They must be expanded jointly; expanding only the second equation would retain a spurious shrinkage term.

For completeness, derivative bounds follow from a resolvent calculation. Apply the symmetric dilation
\[
 \mathcal A(Z)=\begin{pmatrix}0&Z\\ Z^{\top}&0\end{pmatrix}
\]
and surround its \(2r\) nonzero signal eigenvalues by disjoint contours at distance \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}/4\) from zero. Differentiating
\[
 \Pi(Z)=\frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm i}\int_{\mathcal C}
 (zI-\mathcal A(Z))^{-1}\,dz
\]
twice and three times, and multiplying the resulting singular-space projectors by \(Z\), gives
\[
 \|D^2\mathcal P_r(M_0)[A,B]\|_F
 \le \frac C{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}}\|A\|_F\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}+(A\leftrightarrow B),
\tag{16}
\]
\[
 \|D^3\mathcal P_r(M_0)[A,B,C]\|_F
 \le \frac C{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}^2}
 \sum_{\mathrm{cyc}}\|A\|_F\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|C\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{17}
\]
The same contour calculation with coordinate projections inserted before taking norms gives the rowwise version of (16)--(17); each insertion of the target row or column contributes its local leverage square root. Equations (5)--(6) of the preceding proof therefore prevent the operator-norm loss that would arise from applying (16) to the target cell only at the end.

Put \(T=D\mathcal P_r(M_0)\), \(Q(A)=\tfrac12D^2\mathcal P_r(M_0)[A,A]\), \(h=\langle e,T(e)\rangle_F\), and \(t(E)=[T(E)]_k\). Taylor expansion of the first equation in (15) gives
\[
 (1-h)\delta=t(E)-\lambda S(M_0)_k+[Q(E+\delta e)]_k+u_3+u_{\mathrm{pol}},
\tag{18}
\]
where the integral remainder \(u_3\) uses (17) and \(u_{\mathrm{pol}}=-\lambda\{S(Z)-S(M_0)\}_k\). The second equation and the first equation in (15) also give the exact identity
\[
 \widehat M_{it}-M_{0,k}=\delta+\lambda S(Z)_k.
\tag{19}
\]
At linear order, (18)--(19) imply
\[
 \delta_1=\frac{t(E)-\lambda S(M_0)_k}{1-h},
 \qquad
 \widehat M_{it}-M_{0,k}
 =\frac{t(E)}{1-h}-\frac{\lambda hS(M_0)_k}{1-h}+\cdots .
\tag{20}
\]
Thus the apparent term \(-\lambda S(M_0)_k/(1-h)\) cancels against the \(+\lambda S(Z)_k\) in (19); only the leverage-sized polar term remains. By (5)--(6), \(|S(M_0)_k|\le C\mu r/n\), so its size is at most \(C\lambda(\mu r/n)^2\). This is the claimed order-\(\lambda\) cancellation.

The established complete-tangent lemma identifies
\[
 \frac{t(E)}{1-h}=\ell_{it}(R_{it}\epsilon)
 =\sum_{j\in C(t)}a_{ij,t}\epsilon_{jt}
  +\sum_{s\in S}b_{t,s}\epsilon_{is}
  -\sum_{j\in C(t),s\in S}a_{ij,t}b_{t,s}\epsilon_{js}.
\tag{21}
\]
In particular, the third summand in (21) is a differential term and cannot be moved into a remainder.

Let \(Z_1=E+\ell_{it}(R_{it}\epsilon)e\). Replacing \(\delta\) by its first-order noise part in the quadratic term of (18), and multiplying by \((1-h)^{-1}\), yields exactly
\[
 \frac{[Q(Z_1)]_k}{1-h}
 =q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)
\tag{22}
\]
by \(\mathrm{def:quadratic\mbox{-}drift}\). The residual from replacing \(\delta\) by its first-order part is \(r^{(\mathrm{res})}_{it}\); the integral in (17) defines \(r^{(3)}_{it}\); and all terms containing \(\lambda\) after the cancellation (20), including derivatives of \(S\), define \(r^{(\mathrm{pol})}_{it}\). Equations (16)--(17), the bounded inverse from the active-resolvent lemma, and the rowwise leverage insertions show that these definitions are uniform over the target set. Combining (18)--(22) proves the displayed expansion and the asserted derivative bounds.

added_lemmas.statement:
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), the native and neighborhood-noise-replaced scalar resolvents satisfy
\[
 \left|\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}\Delta^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}\right|
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left[
 \ell_n^4\left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}
 +n^{-3/2}\right\}\right].
\]
In the common-start local chart the native and auxiliary inputs, and hence their selected target values, agree identically whenever \(S\cap\mathcal N_q(t)=\varnothing\); because \(q\) is fixed and \(W\) is consecutive after \(S\), only \(O(q)\) target dates can contribute.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By the definition of \(\epsilon^{(-it)}\), native and auxiliary observed arrays differ only at coordinates \((i,s)\) with \(s\in S\cap\mathcal N_q(t)\). The target coordinate \((i,t)\) is missing and therefore never enters either observed input. Hence
\[
 S\cap\mathcal N_q(t)=\varnothing
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon
 =P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon^{(-it)}.
\tag{23}
\]
The two optimization problems then have identical objective functions. The fixed measurable rule in \(\mathrm{def:native\mbox{-}estimator}\), or equivalently uniqueness of the target value from \(\mathrm{lem:uniform\mbox{-}native\mbox{-}active\mbox{-}resolvent}\), makes their target outputs identical. Their linear and quadratic terms are also identical, so \(\Delta^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}=0\).

Let \(s_0=\max S\). Since \(W\) is an interval and \(s_0<\min W\) by \(\mathrm{ass:window\mbox{-}after\mbox{-}preperiod}\),
\[
 S\cap\mathcal N_q(t)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 1\le t-s_0\le q.
\tag{24}
\]
Thus at most \(q\) dates contribute. For such a date, the perturbation between the two inputs is supported on at most \(2q+1\) cells in one row. Apply the joint expansion of \(\mathrm{lem:native\mbox{-}implicit\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}expansion}\) to the line segment between the two inputs. Its linear and quadratic increments cancel by the definition of \(\Delta^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}\). The third derivative bound (17), the leverage bounds (5)--(6), and the conditional sub-Gaussian moment implication (2) give, after summing over \(i\in G\),
\[
 \left|\frac1g\sum_{i\in G}\Delta^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}\right|
 \le_{\mathbb P} C\ell_n^4
 \left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}+n^{-3/2}\right\}.
\tag{25}
\]
To see the powers in (25), a target-row derivative contributes \(n^{-1/2}\), a second resolvent derivative contributes \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^{-2}\), and the independent-row sum contributes \(g^{-1/2}\asymp n^{-1/2}\); the remaining free donor or preperiod contraction contributes \(n^{1/2}\). Terms with two target leverages are bounded by \(\lambda n^{-2}=O(n^{-3/2}\ell_n)\). The union event from the active-resolvent lemma supplies the displayed \(\ell_n^4\) envelope. These statements follow by applying Cauchy--Schwarz to the coefficient arrays before the row sum, so no independence between different local optimizers is asserted.

Finally sum (25) over the at most \(q\) dates in (24), divide by \(H\ge1\), and absorb the fixed \(q/H\le q\) into the constant. This proves the asserted uniform rate.

added_lemmas.statement:
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), the local quadratic kernels lift to a symmetric matrix \(A_n\) on the common ambient observed array such that
\[
 Q-B_2=\epsilon^{\top}A_n\epsilon
 -\mathbb E[\epsilon^{\top}A_n\epsilon\mid M,\Omega]
\]
and
\[
 |Q-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\ell_n^4}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\sqrt n}\right).
\]
The cubic, polar/regularization, scalar-resolvent, and native--auxiliary terms in the signed aggregate obey
\[
 |R_{\mathrm{agg}}|=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left[
 \ell_n^4\left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}
 +n^{-3/2}\right\}\right].
\]
These are centered aggregate bounds; they do not follow by summing pointwise absolute errors.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For each target, the map \(e\mapsto q_{it}(e)\) is a homogeneous quadratic form. Extend its coefficient matrix by zero from the ordered local observed chart to \(I\times J\), symmetrize it, average over \(gH\), and call the resulting ambient matrix \(A_n\). This construction gives identically
\[
 Q=\epsilon^{\top}A_n\epsilon,
 \qquad B_2=\mathbb E(\epsilon^{\top}A_n\epsilon\mid M,\Omega),
\tag{26}
\]
so the first displayed identity is not an approximation.

The restricted Gram bounds and incoherence imply
\[
 \max_{i,j,t}|a_{ij,t}|\le C/n,
 \qquad \max_{t,s}|b_{t,s}|\le C/n,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j\in C(t)}a_{ij,t}^2+sum_{s\in S}b_{t,s}^2\le C/n.
\tag{27}
\]
The last term of the complete tangent has coefficient \(a_{ij,t}b_{t,s}\), including its negative sign. Substituting all three blocks of \(\ell_{it}\) into the rowwise Hessian bound (16), aggregating equal ambient coordinates before taking norms, and using (27) gives
\[
 \|A_n\|_F^2\le\frac{C}{n\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2},
 \qquad
 \max_u\sum_v |(A_n)_{uv}|le\frac C{n\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}},
 \qquad
 |\operatorname{tr}(A_n\Gamma_q)|\le\frac C{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}.
\tag{28}
\]
If the negative overlap block is omitted, the first two contractions in (28) contain an uncancelled donor--pre row sum; thus (28) specifically uses the complete tangent formula.

Truncate the errors at \(K\ell_n\) and recenter them conditionally. By (2) and a union bound over \(NT=O(n^2)\), the truncation changes (26) with probability \(O(n^{-6})\). Color calendar time by residues modulo \(2q+1\). Within a row, vertices of a fixed color are separated by more than \(q\), and different rows are conditionally independent. In the variance expansion of the centered quadratic form, two coefficient pairs have zero covariance unless the graph formed by their four row--time vertices has no isolated dependency component. Exposing one coefficient pair and then its finitely many possible row/time neighbors, (28) gives
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[(Q-B_2)^2\mid M,\Omega\right]
 \le \frac{C_qK^4\ell_n^8}{n\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}.
\tag{29}
\]
Chebyshev's inequality proves the quadratic bound.

It remains to control the aggregate of the remainders defined in the implicit-expansion lemma. Write every integral Taylor term as a multilinear kernel in the original ambient errors, aggregate equal monomials first, and take its Hoeffding decomposition relative to the independent rows and the \((2q+1)\)-coloring within each row. A nondegenerate degree-one projection changes a tangent coefficient by at most \(C\ell_n^2\sqrt n/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2\); keep this difference inside \(R_{\mathrm{agg}}\), while the declared \(L\) itself remains unchanged. The coefficient calculation using (27), (16)--(17), and \(h_{it}\le C/n\) is
\[
 |\mathbb E R_k|+|R_k-\mathbb E R_k\|_2
 \le C\ell_n^4
 \left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}+n^{-3/2}\right\}
 \rho_n^{,k-3},
 \qquad k\ge3,
\tag{30}
\]
where \(R_k\) denotes the degree-\(k\) projection component and \(\rho_n\) is (10). Equation (30) follows by pairing every nonfree vertex of a degenerate monomial with a vertex in the same row and within \(q\) dates: two free factor sums cost at most \(n\), the aggregate normalization contributes \((gH)^{-1}\), and (27) contributes one \(n^{-1/2}\) for each unpaired tangent leg. The Hessian or third-resolvent denominator contributes \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^{-2}\). Terms containing the residual polar factor have two target leverages and satisfy the second term in braces because
\[
 \lambda n^{-2}=O(n^{-3/2}\ell_n).
\tag{31}
\]
This is a coefficient enumeration of the common ambient polynomial, not a pointwise Lipschitz bound.

Because \(\rho_n=o(1)\), summing (30) over \(k\ge3\), adding the polar and scalar-resolvent pieces from (31), and finally adding the native--auxiliary discrepancy proved in \(\mathrm{lem:neighborhood\mbox{-}native\mbox{-}coupling}\), gives
\[
 |R_{\mathrm{agg}}|le_{\mathbb P}C\ell_n^4
 \left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}+n^{-3/2}\right\}.
\tag{32}
\]
Equations (26), (29), and (32) prove the lemma.

added_lemmas.statement:
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), the pretreatment rank-\(r\) fit satisfies
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{fit}}=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2/\sqrt n).
\]
For every fixed \(|h|\le q\), decomposition into the oracle residual-product average, two signal-error cross terms, and a quadratic signal-error term gives
\[
 |\widehat\gamma(h)-\gamma(h)|
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{m}}+\frac{\log n}{m}
 +\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}+\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}^2\right),
\]
and hence the same bound holds for \(\Delta_\gamma\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
On \(I\times S\), treatment is absent by \(\mathrm{ass:window\mbox{-}after\mbox{-}preperiod}\), \(\mathrm{ass:common\mbox{-}start\mbox{-}mask}\), and causal consistency. Thus
\[
 Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{I\times S}=M_{I\times S}+\epsilon_{I\times S}.
\tag{33}
\]
The preperiod Gram lower bound and exact rank imply
\(\sigma_r(M_{I\times S})\ge c\psi\). Applying the trace-moment calculation (3) to the full preperiod rectangle gives
\[
 \|\epsilon_{I\times S}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{n\ell_n})=o_{\mathbb P}(\psi).
\tag{34}
\]
Use the resolvent expansion (16)--(17) for \(\mathcal P_r\) at \(M_{I\times S}\). The rowwise linear term is the sum of a rank-
\(r\) projection of one noise row and a left-space average across independent rows. From (2), finite \(q\), and a union bound over \(N=O(n)\) rows,
\[
 \max_{i\in I}m^{-1/2}
 \|[D\mathcal P_r(M_{I\times S})\epsilon_{I\times S}]_{i,S}\|_2
 =O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n/\sqrt n).
\tag{35}
\]
The rowwise versions of (16)--(17), (34), and the signal envelope bound the quadratic and integral terms by \(O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2/\sqrt n)\). Combining this with (35) proves
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{fit}}le C_{\mathbb P}\ell_n^2/\sqrt n.
\tag{36}
\]

Put \(d_{is}=\widehat M^{\mathrm{pre}}_{is}-M_{is}\) and define the oracle product average
\[
 \widetilde\gamma(h)=\{N(m-|h|)\}^{-1}
 \sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{s:s+|h|\in S}\epsilon_{is}\epsilon_{i,s+|h|}.
\]
The products have a fixed dependence range no larger than \(2q+|h|\) and uniformly bounded sub-exponential moments by (2). Coloring time into a fixed number of classes and applying the exponential Markov inequality to the product moments gives
\[
 |\widetilde\gamma(h)-\gamma(h)|
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{m}}+\frac{\log n}{m}\right)
\tag{37}
\]
uniformly over the finitely many \(|h|\le q\); this bound is conservative because it does not use the additional pooling over \(N\).

Expanding \(\widehat e_{is}=\epsilon_{is}-d_{is}\) gives exactly
\[
 \widehat\gamma(h)-\widetilde\gamma(h)
 =-\overline{d_s\epsilon_{s+|h|}}
  -\overline{\epsilon_s d_{s+|h|}}
  +\overline{d_sd_{s+|h|}},
\tag{38}
\]
where each bar denotes the same normalized row--time average as above. Cauchy--Schwarz, (36), and the uniform boundedness in probability of the average noise square yield
\[
 |\overline{d_s\epsilon_{s+|h|}}|
 +|\overline{\epsilon_s d_{s+|h|}}|=O_{\mathbb P}(\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}),
 \qquad
 |\overline{d_sd_{s+|h|}}|=O_{\mathbb P}(\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}^2).
\tag{39}
\]
Equations (37)--(39) prove the claimed covariance rate and, because \(q\) is fixed, the maximum-lag rate.

added_lemmas.statement:
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), differentiation of the fitted local singular spaces, leverage, Hessian, and polar factor on the active event, combined with the pretreatment covariance bound, gives
\[
 |\widehat B_2-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt n}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}
 +\frac{\Delta_\gamma}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}\right).
\]
The fitted tangent kernel is relatively stable, and therefore
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^N\|\widehat w_{j\cdot}-w_{j\cdot}\|_2^2
 =o_{\mathbb P}(s^2).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(\bar M^{it}=\mathcal P_r(Z^{it})\). The active-resolvent bound and (16)--(17) imply, uniformly over targets,
\[
 \|\bar M^{it}-M^{it}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 =O_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt n\,\ell_n),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{dist}(\widehat T_{it},T_{it})
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\frac{\sqrt n\,\ell_n}
 {\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}\right)=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{40}
\]
Differentiating the contour resolvent once more shows
\[
 \|D^2\mathcal P_r(\bar M^{it})-D^2\mathcal P_r(M^{it})\|
 \le C\frac{\sqrt n\,\ell_n}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2},
 \quad
 |\widehat h_{it}-h_{it}|le C\frac{\ell_n^2}{n}\rho_n,
\tag{41}
\]
and the identical bound holds for the fitted polar derivative. Since \(1-h_{it}\) and \(1-\widehat h_{it}\) are bounded below by the active-resolvent lemma, inserting (41) into the finite coordinate contraction in \(\mathrm{def:feasible\mbox{-}curvature\mbox{-}correction}\) gives
\[
 |\widehat B_2(\gamma)-B_2|
 \le_{\mathbb P}C\ell_n^4\frac{\sqrt n}
 {\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}.
\tag{42}
\]
For fixed \(q\), the sum of the absolute coordinate coefficients of each quadratic map is bounded by \(C/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\), as in (28). Hence replacing \(\gamma\) by \(\widehat\gamma\) changes the contraction by at most
\[
 |\widehat B_2(\widehat\gamma)-\widehat B_2(\gamma)|
 \le_{\mathbb P} C\Delta_\gamma/psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}.
\tag{43}
\]
Equations (42)--(43) prove the curvature rate.

For the weights, aggregate equal ambient coordinates in the fitted and oracle tangent formulas before taking a norm. Equations (27), (40)--(41), and the bounded scalar inverse imply the relative kernel inequality
\[
 \|\widehat w-w\|_F
 \le_{\mathbb P} C\rho_n\ell_n^2\|w\|_F.
\tag{44}
\]
By (10), \(\rho_n\ell_n^2=o(1)\). The established score-diffuseness lemma gives \(\|w\|_F^2=O(s^2)\). Squaring (44) therefore yields
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^N\|\widehat w_{j\cdot}-w_{j\cdot}\|_2^2
 =o_{\mathbb P}(s^2),
\]
as claimed.

proposed.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), first express all perturbation bounds through \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}=\inf_{(i,t)\in G\times W}\sigma_r(M^{it})\). The native and neighborhood-replaced fits satisfy \(|(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}\Delta^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4\{\sqrt n/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2+n^{-3/2}\})\), and the native estimator obeys \((gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})=L+Q+R_{\mathrm{agg}}\), where \(|Q-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4/(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\sqrt n))\), \(|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4\{\sqrt n/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2+n^{-3/2}\})\), \(\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2/\sqrt n)\), \(\Delta_\gamma=O_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{\log n/m}+\log n/m+\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}+\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}^2)\), \(|\widehat B_2-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4\sqrt n/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2+\Delta_\gamma/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}})\), and \(\sum_i\|\widehat w_{i\cdot}-w_{i\cdot}\|_2^2=o_{\mathbb P}(s^2)\). The term \(R_{\mathrm{agg}}\) contains the cubic, penalty, and native-transfer components fixed by its definition. Since \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\le\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\le\psi\), substitution changes only constants. Under \(\psi\ge n^{1/2+\eta}H^{1/4}\ell_n^8\), the corresponding remainder-to-standard-error ratios are bounded by terms of orders \(\ell_n^4\sqrt H/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\), \(\ell_n^4n\sqrt H/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2\), \(\ell_n^4\sqrt H/n\), and \(\Delta_\gamma\sqrt{nH}/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\), all \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).
proposed.justification: This theorem is the native masked-optimizer bridge from target-specific neighborhood replacement to second-order feasible inference.
proposed.gap: Earlier independent-noise completion and fully observed leave-neighborhood arguments do not provide this scalar-resolvent transfer or its centered growing-window aggregation.
proposed.consumer: The theorem certifies feasible curvature correction and studentization for the estimator used in the SEC Tick Size Pilot panel.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the six native-resolvent, expansion, coupling, aggregate, residual-covariance, and fitted-stability lemmas used by the proof.

prose_updates.tldr: A growing post window makes serial dependence enter deterministic-MNAR panel completion through both the long-run variance of the complete three-block tangent score and a nonzero quadratic rank-projection drift. The native one-missing-cell convex optimizer is localized to a unique active singular-value-thresholding branch, expanded through a scalar resolvent, and coupled to neighborhood-replaced fits. Centered dependency-graph aggregation, pretreatment residual covariance estimation, and fitted Hessian and influence-weight stability then yield a feasible uniform scalar Wald law under the stated weak-signal envelope.

project_justification.fill: The project supplies a local-signal-indexed expansion of the implemented native optimizer, a feasible Hessian--lag covariance correction in each target chart, an influence-weighted residual covariance estimator, an independent-row finite-range central limit theorem, and uniform Wald coverage. The separate exponent-indexed class continues to pose the sharp signal--cohort--window frontier without importing the sufficient envelope into that question.

prose_updates.related_work: Choi and Yuan (2024) provide the deterministic-MNAR subgroup nuclear-norm and rank-projection architecture. Choi and Yuan (2025) provide the fully observed leave-neighbor weak-factor precedent; the present proof transfers neighborhood replacement through the actual masked convex fixed point. Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024) supply only a backup iterative coupling pattern and are not used to replace the estimator. Cen and Lam (2025) motivate residual HAC for missing-factor scores, whereas the present result contracts the fitted rank-projection Hessian and fitted aggregate influence weights against finite-lag covariance. The result is scalar cohort-window inference and does not subsume event-time bands, rank selection, or general dependent matrix completion.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The proof is uniform only under exact known fixed rank, fixed known dependence range, bounded aspect ratios, normalized donor and pretreatment Gram bounds, local-to-global signal comparability, and the stated signal--window envelope. Its aggregate bounds use the one-missing-coordinate common-start chart and fixed-range dependency-graph coloring. They do not establish larger missing local blocks, unknown rank, heterogeneous or long-range covariance, simultaneous event-time bands, or a sharp boundary at the spectral-noise scale.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved class conditions on exact known fixed rank, fixed known dependence range, conditionally independent rows, genuine within-row finite-range block dependence, common stationary covariance, a fixed positive local-to-global signal ratio, a proportional treated cohort, bounded aspect ratios, and explicit donor and pretreatment restricted-Gram bounds. It covers the realized cohort-window contrast for growing windows satisfying the declared joint signal--window envelope, including the proportional-window rank-one calibration with signal order \(n^{4/5}\). It does not claim simultaneous event-time bands, unknown-rank validity, heterogeneous covariance, hidden-block identification, rank-overprojection robustness, or proportional-window inference arbitrarily close to signal order \(n^{1/2}\). The sharp exponent frontier remains a separate open-ended question.
